questions.q: What is Avana?
questions.a:
Avana lets liquidity providers use AMM positions as collateral on Aave V4. A borrower pledges a Uniswap v2 LP token or a Uniswap v3 position to Avana's LP Vault. The borrower then borrows GHO from the Avana Hub through an Avana Borrow Spoke, while the liquidity stays in the pool.

Avana runs on Ethereum mainnet. The Avana Hub and Borrow Spokes are standard Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO.

questions.q: What problem does Avana solve?
questions.a:
Liquidity providers usually have to remove liquidity before they can borrow against their capital. To do that, they exit the pool and give up fee income and their chosen range.

Avana makes supported LP positions usable as collateral. The position stays in the pool. Avana's LPOracle values it, and Aave V4 records it as a vault token that maps 1:1 to the underlying liquidity. The benefit to LPs is capital flexibility, not a guaranteed positive return. Borrowers still bear impermanent loss, price risk, and liquidation risk.

questions.q: How is Avana different from a standard lending market?
questions.a:
Standard lending markets usually treat collateral as simple token balances, such as ETH, BTC, stablecoins, or other ERC-20 assets. Avana is built for collateral that changes over time. An LP position contains two assets and earns fees. Its composition shifts as prices move, it can move out of range, and it needs a specific route to unwind.

For this reason, Avana sets risk per market. Each approved pool, and range where relevant, has its own vault token, collateral factor, caps, and settlement mode. The collateral factor starts from the lower collateral factor of the two pool tokens and is then reduced for pool-specific risk.

questions.q: Which AMMs does Avana support?
questions.a:
Avana supports selected Uniswap v2 LP tokens and Uniswap v3 positions on Ethereum mainnet. For Uniswap v3, only full-range positions and specifically approved ranges are accepted.

Adding Uniswap v4, Curve, Balancer, Aerodrome, other AMMs, or other chains such as Base requires its own technical and risk review and Aave governance approval. Pools are approved one at a time. Avana excludes meme-token pools, pools without enough liquidity history or reliable external pricing, and pools where liquidity removal can be restricted.

questions.q: Does Avana replace the AMM where my liquidity sits?
questions.a:
No. The AMM still handles swaps, pool state, price movement, and fee generation. Avana adds a collateral layer around supported LP positions.

When you pledge an eligible position, Avana's LP Vault holds it, and Avana mints a matching vault token for Aave V4. The liquidity stays in the AMM pool and keeps earning fees while it is in range.

questions.q: How does Avana work at a high level?
questions.a:
Avana works in three steps. First, you pledge a supported LP position to the LP Vault. Second, Avana's Risk Module checks the pool, fee tier, range, oracle availability, and caps. The Aave Adapter then mints a matching vault token and supplies it to the Avana Borrow Spoke for that market. Third, you borrow GHO from the Avana Hub up to your borrowing capacity.

The LP position stays in the AMM. Avana's own contracts handle custody, valuation, and settlement. The Avana Hub and Borrow Spokes are standard, unmodified Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO.

questions.q: Why does Avana use Aave V4 Hub-and-Spoke infrastructure?
questions.a:
Avana uses Aave V4 because it separates shared liquidity from market-specific risk settings. The Avana Hub holds a capped GHO credit line allocated by the Aave DAO. Only approved Borrow Spokes can draw from it.

Each Borrow Spoke covers one market category with its own parameters and caps: stable LP (candidate USDC/USDT), correlated LP (candidate wstETH/WETH), and blue-chip/stable LP (candidate WETH/USDC). The candidates are still being assessed. Avana does not fork or modify Aave V4 code. All Avana-specific logic is in Avana's own contracts.

questions.q: What is a Borrow Spoke?
questions.a:
A Borrow Spoke is a standard Aave V4 Spoke owned by the Aave DAO. It accepts Avana vault tokens as collateral and lets borrowers draw GHO from the Avana Hub. It applies the collateral factor, Collateral Risk, and liquidation parameters for its markets.

Avana uses separate Borrow Spokes because LP positions do not all behave the same way. A stablecoin pair, a correlated pair such as wstETH/WETH, and a blue-chip/stable pair such as WETH/USDC need different collateral factors, caps, and settlement settings.

questions.q: What are Avana vault tokens?
questions.a:
Vault tokens are collateral-only ERC-20 tokens that represent pledged LP positions on Aave V4. Each approved pool, and range where relevant, has its own vault token. Avana mints vault tokens 1:1 with the underlying liquidity when you pledge a position and burns them on withdrawal or settlement. There is no issuance schedule, no emissions, and no exchange rate.

Vault tokens are not user assets and have no secondary market. They move only between the Avana Hub, Borrow Spokes, Position Proxies, the Aave Adapter, and LPVaultSwap. Every outstanding vault token is backed by liquidity held in the LP Vault.

questions.q: What are the main parts of the Avana protocol?
questions.a:
The LP Vault holds pledged LP tokens and NFTs. It records each position's owner, pool, token pair, fee tier, range, and status. The Risk Module checks pool eligibility, the pilot allowlist, position-size limits, and exposure caps. The Collateralization Module mints vault tokens 1:1 with liquidity. The LPOracle prices vault tokens from Chainlink and uses the pool TWAP as a second check.

The Aave Adapter is the borrower's entry point. It handles deposits, borrowing, repayment, and withdrawal through a dedicated Position Proxy for each borrower. LPVaultSwap runs liquidations with flash loans, and AMM settlement adapters remove liquidity and collect fees. Upgradeable Avana contracts sit behind a timelock that Avana Labs cannot bypass. The Aave DAO holds the pause and freeze roles.

questions.q: What happens when I deposit LP collateral?
questions.a:
When you pledge a supported LP position, the Aave Adapter deposits it into the LP Vault. The Risk Module then checks the pool, fee tier, range, oracle availability, and caps. During the pilot, only allowlisted depositors can pledge, and each market has minimum and maximum position sizes.

Once the checks pass, Avana mints a matching vault token and supplies it as collateral on the Borrow Spoke through your Position Proxy. Pledging does not borrow anything by itself. It creates borrowing capacity that you can use while the account stays healthy and GHO liquidity is available.

questions.q: Does my LP position stay active after deposit?
questions.a:
Yes. A pledge changes custody, but it does not remove liquidity from the pool. The pool keeps processing swaps, and your position keeps earning fees. A Uniswap v3 position stops earning fees while it is out of range.

While debt is open, actions that reduce collateral, such as withdrawing, go through the Aave Adapter. They are allowed only if the account stays healthy afterward.

questions.q: Can I claim LP fees while borrowing?
questions.a:
Fees keep accruing to your position while it is in the LP Vault. When you withdraw, the LP Vault releases your LP tokens or NFT together with the uncollected fees.

You can withdraw in full once your debt is repaid, or withdraw part of the position if your account stays healthy afterward.

questions.q: Are LP fees included in collateral value?
questions.a:
The LPOracle values the liquidity in your position. It works out the token amounts from the pool's liquidity math and prices them at Chainlink prices, with no haircut. Uncollected fees are released with the position when you withdraw.

The market's collateral factor sets borrowing limits separately. Avana does not apply a discount to the oracle value.

questions.q: When can I withdraw LP collateral?
questions.a:
You can withdraw in full after your debt is repaid. You can also withdraw part of your collateral if the account stays healthy afterward. The Aave Adapter withdraws and burns the matching vault tokens, and the LP Vault releases your LP tokens or NFT with uncollected fees.

Repaying and withdrawing also work without the Avana frontend, by calling the contracts directly. New borrowing and voluntary withdrawals are blocked while an oracle price is stale or the TWAP check fails. Repayment continues in those cases.

questions.q: How does Avana price LP collateral?
questions.a:
The LPOracle prices each vault token from the pool's liquidity math at Chainlink prices. The formula is value = q0·P0 + q1·P1, where q0 and q1 are the token amounts behind one vault token. For Uniswap v3 positions, the token amounts come from the position's liquidity and range at the reference price.

The oracle reports value with no haircut. The market's collateral factor sets borrowing limits separately. The collateral factor starts from the lower collateral factor of the two pool tokens and is reduced by a pool risk factor.

questions.q: How does Avana reduce oracle and pricing risk?
questions.a:
Chainlink is the valuation reference. The pool's TWAP is a consistency check, not an average or a replacement. If the TWAP moves outside the allowed tolerance, new borrowing and risk-increasing withdrawals are blocked. Repayment and liquidation continue at the Chainlink price.

If the Chainlink feed is stale, the oracle uses the last valid price up to a maximum age. During that time, new borrowing and voluntary withdrawals are blocked. Past the maximum age, liquidations pause until the feed recovers or governance approves a backup feed. Repayment continues.

questions.q: Does Avana discount the oracle value?
questions.a:
Avana does not discount the oracle value itself. Instead, each market's collateral factor accounts for how much value can be recovered in a liquidation. The formula is: LP collateral factor = lower collateral factor of the two pool tokens × pool risk factor.

The pool risk factor reflects range, price sensitivity, pool depth, and expected liquidation costs. Gauntlet has suggested starting as low as 0.25× the lower underlying factor when the borrowed asset is not one of the pool's tokens, such as GHO against WETH/USDC.

questions.q: Why are concentrated liquidity positions treated carefully?
questions.a:
Concentrated liquidity positions change exposure quickly as the price moves. A position can become mostly one asset, or it can move out of range and stop earning fees.

Avana accepts only full-range Uniswap v3 positions and specifically approved ranges, each with its own vault token. The oracle works out the token amounts from the position's liquidity and range. Each market sets its own pool risk factor and settlement mode.

questions.q: What market data does Avana monitor?
questions.a:
Avana's Risk Module checks exposure at the pool, underlying-token, and depositor level, including a limit on the share of a pool's liquidity. Each market has its own pool risk factor, settlement mode, TWAP window, allowed price deviation, and maximum feed age.

Avana Labs publishes weekly usage reports and monthly revenue reports. The reports cover debt and collateral by market, concentration, health factor distribution, and successful, failed, and retried liquidations. They also cover FirstLossReserve usage, bad debt, oracle incidents, credit-line usage, fees, and first-loss resources.

questions.q: How does borrowing work on Avana?
questions.a:
After your position is pledged and its vault token is supplied as collateral, you borrow GHO from the Avana Hub through the Borrow Spoke. The Aave Adapter checks that the price checks pass and that your account stays healthy after the new debt.

The GHO is sent to your wallet, and the debt is recorded on Aave V4. Interest accrues at the base rate × (1 + your risk premium), so your health factor can change even if your collateral does not.

questions.q: How is borrowing capacity calculated?
questions.a:
Borrowing capacity = LP position value × LP collateral factor. The LP collateral factor is the lower collateral factor of the two pool tokens multiplied by a pool risk factor. The pool risk factor reflects range, price sensitivity, pool depth, and expected liquidation costs.

Capacity also depends on existing debt, exposure caps, available GHO liquidity, and oracle checks. For example, a $100,000 full-range WETH/USDC position with a 35% final collateral factor has 35,000 GHO of capacity. These figures are illustrative, not actual market parameters.

questions.q: Why is borrow power lower than my LP value?
questions.a:
Borrowing capacity is lower than LP value because the collateral factor leaves room for price moves, impermanent loss, range changes, and liquidation costs. The oracle reports the full value. The collateral factor sets how much of that value can support debt.

The pool risk factor is applied once and set per market, so the gap between LP value and borrowing capacity differs between markets.

questions.q: What assets can I borrow?
questions.a:
Borrow Spokes lend GHO. The Avana Hub is funded by a capped GHO credit line from the Aave DAO, and governance approves each increase.

Other assets are borrowed through the Avana Lend Spoke, which Aave governance approves separately.

questions.q: Can I borrow against multiple LP positions at once?
questions.a:
Yes. Positions supplied to the same Borrow Spoke back one account, and your risk premium is the weighted average across them. Each position still has its own vault token, collateral factor, and caps.

During the pilot, each account has a limit on the number of positions. The whole account must stay above the required health factor.

questions.q: How do lenders use Avana?
questions.a:
Lending runs through the Avana Lend Spoke, which is separate from the GHO Borrow Spokes. Aave governance approves it separately.

The Lend Spoke lets lenders supply assets directly to the Avana Hub and lets borrowers borrow assets other than GHO. The Avana Hub also holds the Aave DAO's GHO credit line.

questions.q: Where does supplier yield come from?
questions.a:
Through the Lend Spoke, lenders earn interest paid by LP-backed borrowers. Avana Labs keeps a protocol share on lender-funded liquidity. Interest on Aave DAO credit lines still goes to the DAO.

Borrowers pay the Avana Hub base rate plus a risk premium based on their collateral. The base rate is set at or above the Aave Core Hub base rate. Aave governance sets the exact lender terms.

questions.q: Do lenders manage LP collateral themselves?
questions.a:
No. Lenders supply assets to the Avana Hub. They do not choose LP ranges or handle settlement. The Borrow Spokes, LP Vault, and LPVaultSwap handle collateral valuation, health checks, and liquidation.

Aave governance approves the Lend Spoke separately.

questions.q: What protects lender capital?
questions.a:
The Aave DAO's only exposure is the capped GHO credit line, and each increase requires governance approval. Protections include allowlisted depositors during the pilot, per-market caps, collateral factors reduced for pool risk, Chainlink prices with TWAP checks, and liquidations that settle in a single transaction.

If a liquidation uses up the collateral and debt remains, losses are covered in order: first by dedicated first-loss capital, then by revenues committed to loss coverage, and then by the Avana Umbrella. Smart contract, oracle, and liquidation execution risk remain. Avana's contracts are in internal security review, and independent public audits follow.

questions.q: What is the health factor?
questions.a:
Health factor compares the borrowing value of your collateral (value × collateral factor) with your debt. Above 1, the account is healthy. Below 1, it can be liquidated.

In an illustrative example, borrowing 25,000 GHO against a $100,000 WETH/USDC position with a 35% collateral factor gives an initial health factor of 1.40. The interface limits new borrowing at an opening health factor of 1.10.

questions.q: What affects my health factor?
questions.a:
Health factor changes when collateral value, debt, or market parameters change. LP positions change value as token prices move, and Uniswap v3 positions also shift composition within their range. Interest increases debt over time.

Borrowing more lowers your health factor. Repaying debt or adding approved collateral raises it.

questions.q: How does liquidation work on Avana?
questions.a:
An account can be liquidated when its health factor falls below 1. In a single transaction, LPVaultSwap takes a flash loan, repays the debt, and settles the LP collateral behind it. Each market has an approved settlement mode.

Partial settlement covers Uniswap v2 and selected Aerodrome or Uniswap v3 markets. It uses Aave V4's standard liquidation. Normally, only the liquidity needed to restore health is removed, and you keep the rest. Full-position settlement covers most AMMs that use NFTs. It settles the whole position and returns any surplus after debt, fees, and costs to the borrower.

questions.q: Who can liquidate an unhealthy position?
questions.a:
Only approved keepers can call LPVaultSwap, which is the only contract that performs liquidations. Keepers are run by at least two operators: Avana Labs and at least one independent operator.

Opening liquidations to third-party liquidators requires governance approval.

questions.q: What fees apply during liquidation?
questions.a:
In partial-settlement markets, the Aave V4 liquidation bonus pays the keeper reward, execution costs, and Avana's capped liquidation fee. The fee therefore does not add to the borrower's cost. You keep the part of the position that is not removed.

In full-position markets, the keeper reward, costs, and Avana's fee are deducted from the settlement proceeds, up to a per-market maximum percentage of the debt. Any surplus is returned to the borrower.

questions.q: How are new LP pools added?
questions.a:
Avana Labs submits new markets and parameters, and a designated risk reviewer reviews them. Each new collateral pool is published for a two-week review before listing approval.

A pool needs reliable external pricing, enough liquidity history, a way to recover liquidation proceeds under stress, and no restrictions on removing liquidity. Each AMM beyond Uniswap v2 and v3 requires its own review and Aave governance approval.

questions.q: Can risk parameters change over time?
questions.a:
Yes. Risk parameters change as market conditions change. A pool can become less liquid, more volatile, less correlated, or harder to unwind than it was when first listed.

Updates can affect collateral factors, caps, supported pools, pauses, liquidation parameters, and settlement modes. The Aave DAO owns the Hub and Spokes and can pause or freeze markets without Avana Labs. Upgrades to Avana's contracts go through a timelock that Avana Labs cannot bypass, and the DAO can cancel them.

questions.q: Where can I follow governance discussion?
questions.a:
Avana is discussed on the Aave governance forum (governance.aave.com) and then goes to a Snapshot vote. The Ethereum deployment and the GHO funding each go through a follow-up forum review and their own Snapshot vote before AIPs.

Avana Labs also posts updates on X at https://twitter.com/avana_labs.

questions.q: Can interface fees change over time?
questions.a:
Avana Labs earns a frontend fee on the official interface and a liquidation fee. Aave governance sets the exact amounts and approves any later changes. You can avoid the frontend fee by calling the contracts directly.

Interest on the Aave DAO's GHO credit line goes to the DAO, not to Avana Labs.

questions.q: Can I borrow GHO through Avana?
questions.a:
Yes. GHO is the only borrowable asset. You borrow it from the Avana Hub, which holds a capped GHO credit line allocated by the Aave DAO through the GHO Reserve.

GHO debt affects your health factor and accrues interest at the Avana Hub base rate plus your risk premium. All interest revenue attributable to the credit line goes to the Aave DAO.

questions.q: Can GHO be part of LP collateral?
questions.a:
No. The candidate pools are USDC/USDT, wstETH/WETH, and WETH/USDC, and they are still being assessed.

A pool containing GHO can be added later through the same review and governance process as any other new pool.

questions.q: How do I repay GHO debt?
questions.a:
You can repay GHO plus accrued interest at any time unless the market is paused. You repay through the Aave Adapter or by calling the contracts directly. Repayment reduces your debt and raises your health factor.

After full repayment, you can withdraw the position. The LP Vault then releases your LP tokens or NFT with uncollected fees.

questions.q: What is Avana Multiply?
questions.a:
Multiply is a flow in Avana's public sandbox at app.avana.cc. In one workflow, it borrows against LP collateral and reinvests the borrowed funds to increase exposure. The sandbox uses simulated assets and makes no onchain transactions.

Multiply is not part of Avana's Aave V4 markets, which cover GHO borrowing against Uniswap v2 and v3 positions.

questions.q: How is Multiply different from borrowing?
questions.a:
Borrowing gives you assets you can use directly while the account stays healthy. Multiply uses LP-backed borrowing power inside a managed strategy. The borrowed capital goes into approved exposure and is tracked as one position.

Multiply adds leverage. Leverage increases capital efficiency and potential returns, but it also increases downside, liquidation risk, and sensitivity to price movement. The health view matters more, not less, when a position is looped.

questions.q: Do I keep my LP while using Multiply?
questions.a:
Yes. The LP position remains the collateral base while the Multiply position is open. You do not need to exit the AMM position to create leveraged exposure.

The LP position still backs debt, so collateral rules apply, and it can be liquidated if the account becomes unhealthy. Users monitor collateral value, debt, leverage, and liquidation buffer for as long as the loop is open.

questions.q: What limits maximum leverage?
questions.a:
Maximum leverage depends on collateral quality, pool liquidity, volatility, oracle confidence, borrow asset, market caps, and liquidation assumptions. Stable or highly correlated pools usually support different leverage limits than volatile or thin pools.

Avana uses market-specific risk controls. Leverage is limited by the actual LP collateral behind the position, not by a flat multiplier applied to every pool.

questions.q: Can automation help manage position risk?
questions.a:
The sandbox previews automation that monitors account health and triggers actions such as repayment or deleveraging before liquidation. Automation is not part of Avana's Aave V4 markets.

Automation is a risk-management tool, not a guarantee. Market moves, liquidity conditions, transaction delays, oracle updates, and route availability can still affect execution.

questions.q: Can LP collateral support perps-style exposure?
questions.a:
No. Avana covers borrowing GHO against approved Uniswap v2 and v3 positions on Ethereum.

You decide how to use the GHO you borrow, but Avana does not route LP-backed credit into perps or other strategies.

questions.q: What do users monitor after opening a position?
questions.a:
Borrowers monitor health factor, debt, collateral value, borrowing rate, Uniswap v3 range status, and distance to liquidation. In the sandbox Multiply flow, they also see leverage level and unwind controls.

The Avana interface shows these values. You can see when a position is healthy, when it needs attention, and when it is moving closer to liquidation.
